# Code Review Report — PR #253

**Branch:** fix/issue-252-opencode-permission-format  
**Reviewer:** Claude Sonnet 4.6 (Reviewer mode)  
**Date:** 2026-04-30  
**Process:** Shared code review process (`.github/agents/_shared/code-review-process.md`)

---

## Review Summary

This PR converts all 24 `.opencode/agents/` files from the undocumented array-style permission format (`allow: [...]` / `deny: []`) to the documented object-map format (`"*": "deny"` / `"key*": "allow"`), and corrects agent `task:` keys from human-readable display names to file-based identifiers. It also adds `default_agent` and `small_model` to `opencode.json`, and adds a documentation section in `docs/features/opencode-runtime.md` describing the correct format. The fix is complete and correct — all 24 files were updated, all YAML parses without error, and all task IDs resolve to actual agent files on disk. Three files have inconsistent indentation relative to the 21-file corpus standard, and a pre-existing variant divergence was not corrected during the sweep; both are flagged below.

**Files Reviewed:** 26  
**Findings:** 0 Critical, 2 Warning, 2 Suggestion

---

## Findings

### Warning Findings

```
[W-01] Non-standard YAML indentation in three agent files
Category: Style
Severity: Warning
File: .opencode/agents/orchestrator-v3.md, .opencode/agents/coder.md, .opencode/agents/sprint-runner.md
Lines: YAML frontmatter (general)
Description: All 24 agent files parse as valid YAML. However, three files use non-standard
indentation for the bash/task/tools values introduced in this PR:

  File                  bash_indent  task_indent  tools_indent
  orchestrator-v3.md        8            8             4
  coder.md                  6            —             3
  sprint-runner.md          6            6             3

The other 21 files consistently use bash_indent=4, task_indent=4, tools_indent=2.
sprint-runner.md additionally uses 3-space indentation for its permission sub-keys (edit:,
bash:, task:) instead of the standard 2-space, making the entire frontmatter block
non-conformant with the project convention.

All three files are valid YAML that any standard YAML 1.1/1.2 parser will accept correctly.
The risk is not a parse failure but a style inconsistency that will:
  (a) produce noisy future diffs if a uniform-indent formatter is ever run;
  (b) create confusion for humans editing these specific files who expect the 2/4/2 pattern
      seen in the rest of the corpus.
Suggestion: Normalise all three files to use 2-space indentation for permission sub-keys
and 4-space for their values (matching the 21-file standard). This is a style fix only;
no functional change to the permission semantics is involved.
```

```
[W-02] Pre-existing variant divergence not corrected during format sweep
Category: Correctness
Severity: Warning
File: .opencode/agents/auditor-kimi.md, .opencode/agents/auditor-qwen.md,
      .opencode/agents/auditor-glm.md, .opencode/agents/researcher-kimi.md,
      .opencode/agents/researcher-qwen.md, .opencode/agents/researcher-glm.md
Lines: tools: block (frontmatter)
Description: The review checklist requires that model-specific variants remain identical
to their parent agent except for the model: field. A programmatic comparison identified
two pre-existing divergences that this PR did not fix:

  (1) auditor-kimi/qwen/glm.md are missing "chroma/*": true in their tools: block.
      auditor.md has chroma/*, io.github.upstash/context7/*, io.github.tavily-ai/*.
      The three variants have only context7 and tavily — chroma/* is absent.

  (2) researcher-kimi/qwen/glm.md are missing "chroma/*": true in their tools: block.
      researcher.md has tavily, context7, and chroma/*.
      The three variants have only tavily and context7.

  (3) auditor-kimi/qwen/glm.md are missing "echo*": "allow" in their bash: block.
      auditor.md includes echo*; the variants do not.

  (4) researcher-kimi/qwen/glm.md are missing "echo*": "allow" in their bash: block.
      researcher.md includes echo*; the variants do not.

These discrepancies were verified to exist on the development branch before this PR, so
they were not introduced here. However, this PR edited all six variant files as part of
the sweep and had the opportunity to bring them into parity with the parent — it did not
do so.

Impact: auditor and researcher variants that dispatch subagents cannot query ChromaDB
for project context (no chroma/* tool access), and cannot run echo commands (no echo*
bash permission). The parent agents can; the variants running on model-specific paths
cannot.
Suggestion: Add "chroma/*": true and "echo*": "allow" to each of the six variant files
to match the parent agent configuration. These are correctness fixes, not format changes.
```

### Suggestions

```
[S-01] docs/features/opencode-runtime.md: CVE-2026-22813 not named explicitly
Category: Documentation
Severity: Suggestion
File: docs/features/opencode-runtime.md
Lines: Installation section (v1.14.x reference)
Description: The installation section references CVE-2026-22812 by ID and CVSS score,
then covers the second advisory with the phrase "and the other 2026 localhost/web-ui
advisories discussed in the audit report." CVE-2026-22813 (XSS in LLM markdown rendering,
patched in v1.14.x) is documented in the research audit report at GHSA-c83v-7274-4vgp
and was flagged as a Unanimous finding. Naming it explicitly would improve traceability
for developers reading the installation section in isolation.
Suggestion: Expand to:
  "the patch for CVE-2026-22812 (CVSS 8.8, unauthenticated local shell execution) and
  CVE-2026-22813 (XSS in LLM markdown rendering)"
```

```
[S-02] synthesizing-reviewer.md has no tools: block — chroma access not available
Category: Correctness
Severity: Suggestion
File: .opencode/agents/synthesizing-reviewer.md
Lines: frontmatter (tools section absent)
Description: The synthesizing-reviewer agent has no tools: block. Its task is to read
three raw review reports from disk (via bash cat/grep) and produce a synthesis — it
does not need ChromaDB for this workflow. The absence is intentional and correct for
the current design.

However, if the synthesizing reviewer ever needs to recall project patterns or gotchas
from the knowledge base to apply consistent severity thresholds, it has no chroma access.
This is a low-priority gap; document it here for awareness only.
Suggestion: Consider adding "chroma/*": true if ChromaDB-assisted pattern recall is
desired during synthesis. Not required for current workflow correctness.
```

## Phase 2 — Code Review

### opencode.json

`default_agent: "orchestrator-v3"` — value matches the filename (`orchestrator-v3.md`). Consistent with the task ID convention used throughout the agent files. ✅

`small_model: "openrouter/qwen/qwen3.6-plus"` — matches the model ID registered under `provider.openrouter.models` in the same file, and confirmed as an active OpenRouter model in the research audit (U-04). The documentation correctly describes this field as routing low-cost background work to a cheaper model tier. ✅

`$schema: "https://opencode.ai/config.json"` — schema URL unchanged; continues to validate the full config block. ✅

### Agent frontmatter — format correctness

**bash: section:** All files now use `"*": "deny"` as the default-deny sentinel followed by explicit `"glob*": "allow"` entries. Pattern is consistent with the documented Opencode permission object-map format (research audit U-02 fix). ✅

**task: section:** All files now use file-ID keys (`"test-writer"`, `"coder"`, `"synthesizing-reviewer"`, etc.) derived from the filename without `.md`. Display-name keys (`"Test Writer"`, `"Coder"`, etc.) are fully eliminated (research audit U-03 fix). ✅

**edit: section (planner.md):** Path-scoped edit permissions converted from array format to object-map:
```yaml
"docs/planning/**": "allow"
".github/notes/**": "allow"
"**": "deny"
```
Matches the documented format (research audit M-02 fix). ✅

**tools: section:** All tools entries converted from `"allow"` string values to `true` boolean values. Pattern matches the documented MCP scoping format (research audit M-01 fix). ✅

**task: deny scalar forms preserved:** `synthesizing-reviewer.md` and `coder.md` retain `task: deny` as scalar strings. The documentation explicitly states scalar forms remain valid when an agent must never dispatch subagents. ✅

### Dispatch contract completeness

The `orchestrator-v3` task allow-list was compared against the agent's body text:
- All agents named in body text (`coder`, `test-writer`, `researcher`, `documenter`, `reviewer-kimi`, `reviewer-qwen`, `reviewer-glm`, `synthesizing-reviewer`, `reflection`, `browser`) appear in the task allow-list. ✅
- `pr-reviewer` appears in the allow-list and in the description field but has no explicit dispatch step — appropriate for an ad-hoc dispatch agent ("Invoked directly by the user or by the Orchestrator for ad-hoc GitHub PR reviews"). ✅

## Phase 4 — Security Review

No security issues introduced. The permission format change makes agent security postures more explicit and correct — the old undocumented array format may have failed open (no restrictions applied) where the new map format enforces deny-by-default. ✅

The `default_agent` value (`orchestrator-v3`) and `small_model` value (`openrouter/qwen/qwen3.6-plus`) are both project-controlled strings; no credential or secret exposure. ✅

## Phase 7 — Documentation Review

`docs/features/opencode-runtime.md` was updated in the same PR as the agent fixes. The documentation:

- Correctly describes the new `permission.bash` object-map format with a `"*": "deny"` sentinel pattern. ✅
- Correctly describes the new `permission.task` format with file-ID keys. ✅
- Correctly states scalar forms (`task: deny`) remain valid for agents that never dispatch. ✅
- Correctly describes `tools:` values as booleans (`true`/`false`), not permission strings. ✅
- Accurately embeds the full `opencode.json` contents as a code block — verified to match the actual file on disk. ✅
- The directory layout tree lists all 24 agents. Count verified against disk listing. ✅
- Version requirement (`v1.14.x` minimum) correctly referenced with security rationale. ✅
- CVE-2026-22812 explicitly named; CVE-2026-22813 covered implicitly. See S-01.

## Overall Assessment

This PR correctly and completely fixes the permission format issue identified in the research audit. All 24 agent files have been updated, the YAML is valid in every file, task dispatch IDs resolve to real agent files, the `opencode.json` additions are consistent with the research findings, and the documentation accurately describes the new format. No critical defects were found.

The two Warnings are pre-existing quality issues (inconsistent indentation in 3 files; missing `chroma/*` and `echo*` in 6 variant files) that the PR did not introduce but also did not correct while passing through. They are safe to defer to a follow-up issue but should not block merge. The S-01 documentation suggestion is cosmetic. The PR is ready for merge.
